The **2014–15 Missouri State Lady Bears basketball team** represented **Missouri State University** during the **2014–15 NCAA Division I women's basketball season**. The Lady Bears, led by **head coach Kellie Harper** (in her sixth and final season at Missouri State before leaving for Tennessee), competed in the **Missouri Valley Conference (MVC)** and played their home games at **JQH Arena** in Springfield, Missouri.

Here’s a detailed breakdown of the team’s season:

---

### **Key Team Information**
- **Head Coach:** Kellie Harper (6th season)
- **Assistant Coaches:** Jackie Stiles, Brittany Carter, Tisha Hill
- **Home Arena:** JQH Arena (capacity: 11,000)
- **Conference:** Missouri Valley Conference (MVC)
- **Record:** **23–11 (14–4 MVC, 2nd place)**
- **Postseason:** **WNIT (Women’s National Invitation Tournament) – Second Round**

---

### **Roster & Key Players**
The 2014–15 team featured a mix of experienced upperclassmen and talented newcomers. Some of the standout players included:

| **Player**            | **Position** | **Year** | **Key Stats (2014–15)** |
|-----------------------|-------------|----------|-------------------------|
| **Alexis Prince**     | G/F         | Senior   | 14.2 PPG, 5.8 RPG, 2.1 APG |
| **Tyler Cook**        | G           | Senior   | 12.1 PPG, 3.8 RPG, 3.2 APG |
| **Hannah Wilkerson**  | G           | Junior   | 10.5 PPG, 3.1 RPG, 2.4 APG |
| **Lacy Ellis**        | F           | Senior   | 8.7 PPG, 6.1 RPG, 1.2 BPG |
| **Camille Dorris**    | G           | Sophomore| 7.8 PPG, 2.3 RPG, 1.8 APG |
| **Megan Pearson**     | F           | Junior   | 6.5 PPG, 4.2 RPG |
| **Ronni Williams**    | F           | Freshman | 5.1 PPG, 3.8 RPG (future star) |

**Notable Freshmen:**
- **Ronni Williams** (later transferred to Florida) showed promise as a versatile forward.
- **Keke Calloway** (later transferred to Georgia) was another young talent.

---

### **Season Overview**
#### **Non-Conference Play (7–4)**
- The Lady Bears started the season with a **7–4 non-conference record**, facing tough competition.
- **Key Wins:**
  - **Wichita State (68–63)** – Early MVC preview.
  - **Arkansas (62–58)** – Upset over an SEC team.
  - **Oral Roberts (78–65)** – Strong offensive performance.
- **Key Losses:**
  - **#10 Texas A&M (53–75)** – Ranked opponent.
  - **Kansas State (58–72)** – Close game but fell short.
  - **Iowa State (56–70)** – Another Power 5 loss.

#### **Missouri Valley Conference Play (14–4, 2nd Place)**
- Missouri State finished **second in the MVC** behind **Wichita State (16–2)**.
- **Key Games:**
  - **Split with Wichita State** (Lost 68–72 at home, won 73–69 on the road).
  - **Swept Drake (14–4 MVC)** and **Northern Iowa (12–6 MVC)**.
  - **Lost to Evansville (6–12 MVC) 65–68** in a surprising upset.
- **MVC Tournament:**
  - **Quarterfinal:** Defeated **Southern Illinois (71–52)**.
  - **Semifinal:** Lost to **Wichita State (58–67)** in a close game.

#### **Postseason: WNIT (Women’s National Invitation Tournament)**
- The Lady Bears earned a **WNIT bid** (their third in four years under Harper).
- **First Round:** Defeated **Saint Louis (68–63)** in a tight game.
- **Second Round:** Lost to **Iowa (62–75)** – Ended their season.

---

### **Season Highlights & Achievements**
✅ **23 Wins** – One of the best seasons in program history at the time.
✅ **WNIT Appearance** – Third straight postseason bid (2013, 2014, 2015).
✅ **Alexis Prince** – **First-Team All-MVC**, MVC All-Tournament Team.
✅ **Tyler Cook** – **Second-Team All-MVC**, MVC All-Tournament Team.
✅ **Lacy Ellis** – **MVC Defensive Player of the Year** (led the team in rebounds & blocks).
✅ **Kellie Harper** – **MVC Coach of the Year** (final season at Missouri State before leaving for Tennessee).

---

### **Coaching Change & Aftermath**
- **Kellie Harper left after the season** to become the head coach at **Tennessee** (her alma mater).
- **Assistant Coach Jackie Stiles** (a former WNBA star and Missouri State legend) was promoted to **interim head coach** before later taking the permanent job.
- The 2014–15 team set the stage for future success, including **MVC regular-season titles in 2016 and 2019** under Stiles.

---

### **Legacy of the 2014–15 Team**
- This was one of the most **talented and competitive teams** in Missouri State history, finishing with **23 wins** and a **top-2 MVC finish**.
- The team was known for its **balanced scoring**, **strong defense**, and **clutch performances** in big games.
- Several players (like **Ronni Williams**) went on to have successful careers elsewhere.
- The season marked the **end of an era** for Harper at Missouri State but laid the foundation for future success under Jackie Stiles.

---

### **Final Thoughts**
The **2014–15 Missouri State Lady Bears** were a **fun, gritty, and competitive team** that came close to winning the MVC but fell just short. Their **WNIT run** and **individual accolades** made it a memorable season, and they remain one of the most **successful teams in program history** in terms of wins and postseason success.
